tldr: Distills an optimized agent harness into model weights: a harnessing agent reviews and rewrites the student's responses at training time, and SFT on those trajectories moves the behavior into the model — so the specialized harness can be removed at deployment and the gains remain (23.3% → 44.3% macro-average, beating the 41.7% the base model gets with the optimized harness still attached).
method: Three stages. (1) Evolve a student-side harness h* on training tasks, then Adapt it into a private reference harness K for a separate harnessing agent — e.g. a middleware rule that blocks risky actions becomes a review-time warning. (2) Agent-as-harness trajectory collection: the student runs under a fixed minimal target harness h (one bash tool, fixed system prompt); before any response is executed, the harnessing agent reviews it against K and either PASSes it unchanged or REPLACEs it with a complete response valid in h's action space; only the accepted response enters the student-visible trajectory and the review stays private. (3) SFT on the reviewed rollouts (masking reviewer-perspective reasoning), then deploy under h alone.
results: Agent-as-harness beats code-as-harness on frontier models: 81.1% vs 78.1% averaged across six benchmark–model settings.

Harness distillation into Qwen3.5-9B lifts macro-average task success from 23.3% to 44.3% across SpreadsheetBench / AppWorld / USPTO — above the 41.7% the base model reaches with the evolved harness h* still attached (a 90.1% relative improvement).
82.3% average recovery of 28 harness-induced behavior patterns (memory, skill, tool, middleware) absent from the base model — direct evidence the behavior moved into the weights.
Supervision-source ablation: harness-guided review (30%) far exceeds direct trajectories from a stronger model, trajectories under h*, review without K, or review given only the task answer (3–15%).
advantages: Distillation across incompatible action spaces, which is what makes the rest work: trajectories collected under h* are unusable for imitation under h — SFT on them drops the student from 12% to 3% because the model emits harness-tool calls that h does not provide. Agent-as-harness sidesteps the mismatch by expressing every correction as a complete response valid in h, and reaches 30% from the same base.

Removes the harness entirely rather than routing around it: the deployed system is (π_θ̂, h) with no h*, K, or harnessing agent, and the distilled 9B still beats the base model with h* mounted (44.3% vs 41.7%). Neither general-purpose harness helps that base model at all (DeepAgents 20.5% and Claude Code 15.9% vs 23.3% under minimal h), so the gain is specific to the evolved harness's behavior, now in the weights.

Shows collection success does not predict distillation value: review with oracle answers scores 98.6% collection success but yields a 15% student, while K — which contains no task answers and reaches only 59.4% collection success — yields 30%. The signal is procedural guidance the student can execute independently, not correct answers.

The 81.1% vs 78.1% margin cannot be credited to a stronger supervisor: in §4.2 the same model plays both student and harnessing agent, and with an empty K the same wrapper averages only 69.2%, so the gain comes from the adapted reference harness rather than from review per se.
limitations: Depends on a capable harnessing model; with weaker models review can become harmful and agent-as-harness loses its edge over code-as-harness.
Reviewing every proposal multiplies collection cost (an extra model call per step; ~2.4× USPTO latency) — though the overhead is absent after distillation.

Some harness mechanisms (notably context management) are not fully expressible as student responses, and SFT may not fully internalize deep domain knowledge — so it narrows rather than removes the need for a harness.
fits: The clearest demonstration yet of the harness→weight transfer rsif's policy surface points at: an optimized harness's induced behaviors are distilled into model parameters via a temporary reviewing agent, then the harness is removed. rsif evolves its artifacts directly under programmatic gates; Harness-Zero shows the complementary move — that harness gains can be converted into training signal and folded back into weights, collapsing a harness collection into one minimal harness. Its agent-as-harness-beats-code-as-harness result is the key empirical claim to weigh against rsif's code-as-substrate stance.
reading: Read §3 for the evolve→adapt→review→SFT pipeline (the PASS/REPLACE review boundary and why the review stays private), then §4.2's agent-as-harness vs code-as-harness comparison and §4.4's supervision-source ablation (30% vs 3–15%) as the tightest evidence for review quality.
